Consider the following two syntax-directed definitions SDD1 and SDD2 for type declarations.

**SDD1**

| Grammar (G1) | Semantic Rules |
|---|---|
| $D \to T\ V$ | $D.\mathit{type} = T.\mathit{type}$; $\ V.\mathit{type} = T.\mathit{type}$ |
| $T \to \mathit{int}$ | $T.\mathit{type} = \mathit{int}$ |
| $T \to \mathit{float}$ | $T.\mathit{type} = \mathit{float}$ |
| $V \to V_1\ \mathit{id}$ | $V_1.\mathit{type} = V.\mathit{type}$; $\ \mathit{put}(\mathit{id}.\mathit{entry}, V.\mathit{type})$ |
| $V \to \mathit{id}$ | $\mathit{put}(\mathit{id}.\mathit{entry}, V.\mathit{type})$ |

**SDD2**

| Grammar (G2) | Semantic Rules |
|---|---|
| $D \to D_1\ \mathit{id}$ | $D.\mathit{type} = D_1.\mathit{type}$; $\ \mathit{put}(\mathit{id}.\mathit{entry}, D_1.\mathit{type})$ |
| $D \to T\ \mathit{id}$ | $D.\mathit{type} = T.\mathit{type}$; $\ \mathit{put}(\mathit{id}.\mathit{entry}, T.\mathit{type})$ |
| $T \to \mathit{int}$ | $T.\mathit{type} = \mathit{int}$ |
| $T \to \mathit{float}$ | $T.\mathit{type} = \mathit{float}$ |

$D$ is the start symbol, and $\mathit{int}$, $\mathit{float}$ and $\mathit{id}$ are the three terminals. The non-terminal $V_1$ is the same as $V$ and the non-terminal $D_1$ is the same as $D$. Here, the subscript is used to differentiate the grammar symbols on the two sides of a production. The function $\mathit{put}$ updates the symbol table with the type information for an identifier.

Let P and Q be the languages specified by grammars G1 and G2, respectively.

Which of the following statements is/are true?
